translations.hi: भविष्य की आय और व्यय के लिए वित्तीय योजना
translations.ja: 将来の収入と支出に関する財務計画
translations.ko: 미래의 수입과 지출에 대한 재정 계획
translations.ps: د راتلونکي عاید او لګښت لپاره مالي پلان
translations.ro: plan financiar pentru venituri și cheltuieli viitoare
translations.ru: финансовый план будущих доходов и расходов
translations.ta: எதிர்கால வருமானம் மற்றும் செலவுக்கான நிதித் திட்டம்
translations.tl: planong pinansyal para sa hinaharap na kita at gastos
translations.ur: مستقبل کی آمدنی اور اخراجات کے لیے مالی منصوبہ
translations.vi: kế hoạch tài chính cho thu nhập và chi tiêu tương lai
translations.zh-Hans: 关于未来收入与支出的财务计划
translations.zh-Hant: 關於未來收入與支出的財務計劃

words.meaning: A plan for how money will be earned and spent.
words.example: Set out a weekly budget with income in one column and spending in the other.

words.meaning: A business that sells goods straight to customers.
words.example: The retailer buys at the cost price and sells at a mark-up.

words.meaning: A person who buys and uses goods or services.
words.example: The consumer pays the marked price plus 10% GST.

words.meaning: A document listing goods or services supplied and the amount owed.
words.example: The invoice shows the total before the 10% GST is added.

words.meaning: A document showing what was bought and how much was paid.
words.example: Check the receipt to see how much GST you paid.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapter 4A–4C: Length, perimeter and area

translations.vi: trạng thái hoặc tính chất của

words.meaning: How long something is, measured in units such as mm, cm or m.
words.example: Measure the length of each side in centimetres.

words.meaning: The total distance around the outside edge of a 2D shape.
words.example: Add all four sides to find the perimeter of the rectangle.

words.meaning: The distance all the way around a circle.
words.example: Use C = 2πr to find the circumference.

words.meaning: The amount of flat surface a 2D shape covers, measured in square units.
words.example: The area of this rectangle is 12 cm².

words.meaning: A shape made by joining two or more simpler shapes together.
words.example: Split the composite shape into a rectangle and a triangle first.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapter 4D–4F: Area of special shapes

words.meaning: The side of a shape that the height is measured from in an area formula.
words.example: Multiply the base by the perpendicular height, then halve it.

words.meaning: The height of a shape measured at a right angle to the base.
words.example: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanted side.

words.meaning: The distance from the centre of a circle out to its edge.
words.example: The radius is half the diameter.

words.meaning: The distance right across a circle, passing through its centre.
words.example: The diameter is twice the radius.

words.meaning: The special number close to 3.14159 that is used in every circle formula.
words.example: Leave your answer in terms of pi rather than rounding.

words.meaning: A slice of a circle between two radii and an arc.
words.example: Find the area of the sector by taking a fraction of the whole circle.

words.meaning: A curved part of the circumference of a circle.
words.example: The arc length is a fraction of the whole circumference.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapter 4G–4J: Surface area, volume and time

words.meaning: The total area of all the outer faces of a 3D shape.
words.example: Add the areas of all six faces to find the surface area of the cube.

words.meaning: A 3D shape with two identical parallel end faces and flat sides.
words.example: The volume of a prism is the end area times the length.

words.meaning: A 3D shape with two identical circular ends joined by a curved surface.
words.example: Find the volume of the cylinder using V = πr²h.

words.meaning: The amount of space inside a 3D shape, measured in cubic units.
words.example: The volume of this box is 60 cm³.

words.meaning: The amount of liquid or gas a container can hold, usually in millilitres or litres.
words.example: A volume of 1000 cm³ is a capacity of one litre.

words.meaning: The units used to measure volume, such as cm³ or m³.
words.example: Give the volume answer in cubic units, not square units.

words.meaning: A way of writing the time from 00:00 to 23:59 with no am or pm.
words.example: Half past seven in the evening is 19:30 in 24-hour time.

words.meaning: A region of the world that keeps the same standard clock time.
words.example: Perth is in a different time zone from Melbourne.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapter 4K–4M: Pythagoras' theorem

words.meaning: A triangle with one angle of exactly 90°.
words.example: Label the sides of the right-angled triangle a, b and c.

words.meaning: The longest side of a right-angled triangle, always opposite the right angle.
words.example: The hypotenuse is always opposite the 90° angle.

words.meaning: The rule that in a right-angled triangle a² + b² = c².
words.example: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find the missing side.

words.meaning: A set of three whole numbers that fit Pythagoras' theorem exactly.
words.example: The numbers 3, 4 and 5 make the best-known Pythagorean triple.

words.meaning: The number that gives a certain value when it is multiplied by itself.
words.example: Take the square root of 144 to get 12.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 5J–5K: Index laws

words.meaning: The small raised number that tells you how many times to multiply the base by itself.
words.example: In 2³ the index is 3, so work out 2 × 2 × 2.

words.meaning: The number or pronumeral that is multiplied by itself in a power.
words.example: In 5⁴ the base is 5.

words.meaning: The rules for simplifying powers, such as adding the indices when you multiply powers with the same base.
words.example: Use the index laws to simplify a⁵ × a³.

words.meaning: Any number except 0, raised to the power of 0, equals 1.
words.example: By the zero index rule, 7⁰ = 1.

words.meaning: Raising a power to another power, which you do by multiplying the two indices.
words.example: For a power of a power, (x²)³ becomes x⁶.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 6A–6G: Ratios, rates and scale

words.meaning: A comparison of two or more amounts of the same kind, written with a colon.
words.example: Write the ratio of red counters to blue counters as 3:5.

words.meaning: Dividing both parts of a ratio by a common factor to reach the smallest whole numbers.
words.example: Simplifying a ratio, 10:15 becomes 2:3.

words.meaning: Different ratios that describe exactly the same comparison.
words.example: 1:2 and 4:8 are equivalent ratios.

words.meaning: An accurate drawing of a real object, made larger or smaller by a stated scale.
words.example: On this scale drawing, 1 cm stands for 2 m.

words.meaning: The number you multiply a length by to get from one shape or drawing to another.
words.example: The scale factor is 3, so every side is three times longer.

words.meaning: A comparison of two different kinds of quantity, such as kilometres per hour.
words.example: Write 240 km in 3 hours as a rate.

words.meaning: A rate written so that the second quantity is exactly 1.
words.example: Divide to find the unit rate: $12 for 4 kg is $3 per kg.

words.meaning: How fast something moves — the rate at which distance changes with time.
words.example: Find the speed if a car travels 150 km in 2 hours.

words.meaning: The total distance travelled divided by the total time taken.
words.example: Her average speed for the whole trip was 60 km/h.

translations.hi: किसी काम को करने का तरीका
translations.ro: un mod de a face ceva
translations.tl: paraan ng paggawa ng isang bagay
translations.ur: کسی کام کو کرنے کا طریقہ
translations.vi: cách làm một việc gì đó

words.meaning: Finding the value of one unit first, then multiplying to find the value you need.
words.example: Use the unitary method: if 5 pens cost $10, one pen costs $2.

translations.vi: phương pháp quy về đơn vị
translations.es: método de reducción a la unidad

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 7F–7H: Quadratics, formulas and applications

words.meaning: Describes an expression where the highest power of the letter is 2.
words.example: Solve this quadratic equation by factorising.

words.meaning: A rule written with letters that you use to work something out.
words.example: Use the formula to find the area.

words.meaning: How two amounts are connected, shown by a rule or a graph.
words.example: Describe the relationship between x and y.

words.meaning: Using maths you have learned to solve a real-life problem.
words.example: This question is an application of linear equations.

words.meaning: An equation in which the highest power of the pronumeral is 2.
words.example: x² + 3x = 10 is a quadratic equation.

words.meaning: The pronumeral standing alone on one side of a formula.
words.example: Make l the subject of the formula A = l × w.

words.meaning: The quantity you choose or change first in a relationship.
words.example: Time is the independent variable, so plot it along the x-axis.

words.meaning: The quantity whose value depends on the independent variable.
words.example: Distance is the dependent variable, so plot it up the y-axis.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 8A–8C: Graphs, tables and frequency

words.meaning: The number of times a particular value or result appears in a data set.
words.example: The frequency of the score 7 is four.

words.meaning: A table that records how often each value, or each group of values, occurs.
words.example: Put the results into a frequency table before you graph them.

words.meaning: A quick way of counting with marks, usually grouped in fives.
words.example: Keep a tally as you count each colour.

words.meaning: A graph that uses vertical bars to show and compare quantities.
words.example: Draw a column graph of the frequencies.

words.meaning: A circle cut into slices to show how a total is shared between categories.
words.example: Each slice of the pie chart stands for one sport.

words.meaning: Data sorted into named groups instead of numbers, such as eye colour.
words.example: Favourite sport is categorical data, so use a column graph.

words.meaning: Data made of numbers that can be counted or measured.
words.example: Height in centimetres is numerical data.

words.meaning: Numerical data that can only take separate, exact values, such as the number of siblings.
words.example: You can have 2 pets or 3, but not 2.5, so pet numbers are discrete data.

words.meaning: Numerical data that can take any value in a range, such as height or time.
words.example: Time in seconds is continuous data.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 8D–8F: Measures of centre and spread; sampling

words.meaning: The average: add every value, then divide by how many values there are.
words.example: Find the mean of 4, 7 and 10.

words.meaning: The middle value of a data set once it is put in order.
words.example: Put the marks in order first, then read off the median.

words.meaning: The value that appears most often in a data set.
words.example: The mode is 6 because it appears five times.

words.meaning: The difference between the highest and the lowest value in a data set.
words.example: The range is 95 - 40, which is 55.

words.meaning: A value that sits far above or far below the rest of the data.
words.example: The score of 2 is an outlier and it drags the mean down.

words.meaning: The spread of the middle half of the data, once the top and bottom quarters are removed.
words.example: Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile to get the interquartile range (IQR).

words.meaning: The value a quarter of the way down from the top, and the value a quarter up from the bottom, of ordered data.
words.example: Split the ordered data in half, then find the upper quartile and lower quartile.

translations.vi: tứ phân vị trên và dưới

words.meaning: A smaller group chosen to stand for a larger population.
words.example: Survey a sample of 50 students instead of the whole school.

words.meaning: The whole group being studied, not just the part you survey.
words.example: The population here is every student in the school.

translations.fr: transformé en / ayant la forme de
translations.ur: میں تبدیل شدہ / شکل رکھنے والا

words.meaning: A sample that unfairly favours one result, so it does not represent the population.
words.example: Asking only the football team gives a biased sample.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 8G–8K: Probability

words.meaning: A measure of how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
words.example: The probability of rolling a 4 on a fair dice is 1/6.

words.meaning: The list of every possible outcome of an experiment.
words.example: The sample space for one coin toss is heads, tails.

words.meaning: One or more outcomes from the sample space that you are interested in.
words.example: The event 'an even number' has three outcomes.

words.meaning: Probability worked out from the results you actually got when you ran the experiment.
words.example: Heads came up 27 times in 50, so the experimental probability is 0.54.

words.meaning: Probability worked out by reasoning about equally likely outcomes, without doing an experiment.
words.example: The theoretical probability of heads is 0.5.

words.meaning: Two events where exactly one of them must happen, so their probabilities add to 1.
words.example: Rain and no rain are complementary events.

words.meaning: Events that cannot both happen at the same time.
words.example: Rolling a 2 and rolling a 5 on one dice are mutually exclusive events.

words.meaning: A branching diagram that shows every possible outcome of two or more events.
words.example: Draw a tree diagram for tossing a coin twice.

words.meaning: A diagram of overlapping circles showing how groups of items overlap.
words.example: The Venn diagram shows students who play soccer, basketball, or both.

words.meaning: A table that sorts data by two different categories at once.
words.example: The two-way table sorts students by year level and by sport.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 9A–9J: Linear relationships and gradient

words.meaning: The number plane made by a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis.
words.example: Plot the point (3, 5) on the Cartesian plane.

words.meaning: A connection between two variables that makes a straight line when you graph it.
words.example: y = 2x + 1 is a linear relationship.

words.meaning: In maths, an equation telling you how to get one variable from another — not an order you must obey.
words.example: Find the rule that turns each x value into its y value.

words.meaning: The point where a line or curve crosses the x-axis, where y is 0.
words.example: Let y = 0 to find the x-intercept.

translations.ro: abscisa la origine (intersecția cu axa Ox)
translations.es: abscisa al origen (corte con el eje x)

words.meaning: The point where a line or curve crosses the y-axis, where x is 0.
words.example: In y = 3x + 4, the y-intercept is 4.

words.meaning: An equation whose graph is a straight line.
words.example: y = 5x - 2 is a linear equation.

words.meaning: A measure of how steep a line is, worked out as rise over run.
words.example: A gradient of 2 means the line goes up 2 for every 1 across.

words.meaning: The vertical change between two points on a line.
words.example: The rise is 6 and the run is 3, so the gradient is 2.

words.meaning: The horizontal change between two points on a line.
words.example: Count the run across before you divide the rise by it.

words.meaning: Writing a linear equation as y = mx + c, where m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept.
words.example: Rearrange 2y = 6x + 8 into gradient–intercept form.

translations.vi: dạng hệ số góc–tung độ gốc

words.meaning: A graph that is not a straight line, such as a curve.
words.example: y = x² gives a non-linear graph shaped like a parabola.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapters 10A–10I: Transformations, congruence and similarity

words.meaning: A change to a shape's position, size, or the way it faces.
words.example: Name the transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.

words.meaning: Flipping a shape over a mirror line to make a mirror image.
words.example: Draw the reflection of the shape in the y-axis.

words.meaning: Sliding a shape to a new position without turning it or flipping it.
words.example: Describe the translation as 3 units right and 2 units down.

words.meaning: Turning a shape around a fixed point by a given angle.
words.example: Draw the shape after a rotation of 90° clockwise.

words.meaning: The fixed point a shape turns around when it is rotated.
words.example: Mark the centre of rotation before you turn the shape.

words.meaning: In maths, the new shape you get after a transformation — not a picture.
words.example: Label the image A'B'C' after the reflection.

words.meaning: Shapes that are exactly the same size and exactly the same shape.
words.example: These two rectangles are congruent figures.

words.meaning: Triangles that match exactly, angle for angle and side for side.
words.example: Use the SSS test to show these are congruent triangles.

words.meaning: The sides or angles that match each other in two congruent or similar shapes.
words.example: In congruent shapes, corresponding parts are equal.

words.meaning: A pattern of shapes that fit together with no gaps and no overlaps.
words.example: Regular hexagons make a tessellation.

words.meaning: Shapes with the same shape but not the same size: equal angles, and sides in the same ratio.
words.example: The two rectangles are similar figures with a scale factor of 2.

words.meaning: Triangles with the same angles, whose matching sides are all in the same ratio.
words.example: Use similar triangles to find the missing length.

units.name: Year 8 Maths · Chapter 11: Algorithmic thinking

words.meaning: A set of clear steps, followed in order, that solves a problem.
words.example: Write an algorithm for finding the largest number in a list.

translations.ja: 流れる；なめらかに垂れる

words.meaning: A diagram that shows the steps of an algorithm as boxes joined by arrows.
words.example: Draw a flowchart for the sorting steps.

words.meaning: The information or numbers you put into an algorithm or program.
words.example: The input is the list of unsorted numbers.

words.meaning: The result an algorithm or program produces.
words.example: If the input is 5, the output is 11.

words.meaning: A set of steps carried out one after another in a fixed order.
words.example: Follow the sequence of steps exactly as written.

words.meaning: Putting data into an order, such as smallest to largest.
words.example: Sorting these five numbers takes four passes.

words.meaning: Looking through a set of data to find one particular item.
words.example: Searching an ordered list is much faster than searching a jumbled one.

words.meaning: Using a model or a program to copy a real situation so you can study it.
words.example: Run a simulation of 100 dice rolls.

words.meaning: Finding the smallest or the largest possible value of a quantity, under the conditions given.
words.example: Which box shape uses the least card? That is a minimising problem.

translations.ur: کم سے کم/زیادہ سے زیادہ کرنا

units.name: Narrative — key vocab

words.meaning: A story told as a series of connected events.
words.example: A narrative usually has a beginning, a middle and an end.

words.meaning: The part of a story that gives the background facts the reader needs.
words.example: The exposition tells us where and when the story takes place.

words.meaning: The start of a story that tells who, where and when.
words.example: In the orientation, the writer introduces the main character and the town.

words.meaning: A problem that makes things harder for the characters in a story.
words.example: The complication begins when the character loses the map.

words.meaning: The end of a story, where the main problem is solved.

words.meaning: The last part of a story, where the tangles of the plot are untied and loose ends are sorted out.
words.example: In the denouement we finally learn who was knocking at the window.

words.meaning: A style of story built on horror, mystery, decay and the supernatural.

words.meaning: Chosen to stir a strong feeling in the reader or listener.

words.meaning: A group of words with a subject and a verb that cannot stand alone as a sentence.
words.example: 'When the candle went out' is a dependent clause: it needs a main clause to finish it.

words.meaning: A group of words with a subject and a verb that can stand alone as a complete sentence.
words.example: 'The candle went out' is an independent clause, because it makes sense on its own.

words.example: The refrain returns at the end of every stanza, a little darker each time.

words.meaning: A deep, thoughtful sadness that settles over a person or a place.
words.example: The narrator's melancholy hangs over the whole story.

words.meaning: Beyond the laws of nature: ghosts, curses and things science cannot explain.
words.example: Leave it unclear whether the noise is supernatural or just the wind.

units.name: Telling stories · Sound and word choice

words.meaning: A sound made with the air flowing freely: a, e, i, o, u, and sometimes y.

words.meaning: Repeating the same vowel sound in words that sit close together.

words.meaning: Repeating the same consonant sound in words that sit close together.
words.example: The consonance of 'blank' and 'think' clicks at the end of each word.

words.meaning: Repeating the same sound at the start of neighbouring words.
words.example: 'Silent, sagging shutters' is alliteration a reader can hear.

units.name: Writing stories · Short story structure and style

words.meaning: The opening part of a story, where the characters and the setting are introduced.

words.meaning: The event that sets the main problem of the story going.

words.meaning: The build-up of pressure and danger between the first problem and the climax.

words.meaning: The turning point of a story: the moment of highest tension.
words.example: At the climax the narrator finally opens the door.

words.meaning: How the problem of the story is settled by the end.
words.example: A good resolution answers the story's question without explaining everything.

words.meaning: A story shape that starts in the middle of the action, flashes back to explain, then moves forward again.

words.meaning: The position a story is told from, such as first person or third person.

words.meaning: One of the six traits of writing: how clearly and logically a piece is arranged.

words.meaning: One of the six traits of writing: how precise and effective the words are.

words.meaning: Turning a verb or an adjective into a noun, such as 'decide' becoming 'decision'.

words.meaning: A wide shot at the start of a scene that shows where the action takes place.

words.meaning: A shot taken from far away that shows a character's whole body.

words.meaning: A shot framed from the waist up: the most common shot in a film.
words.example: Most of the conversation is filmed in medium shot.

words.meaning: A shot in which a face fills most of the frame, so the audience reads the emotion.
words.example: The close-up holds on her face just long enough to feel awkward.

words.meaning: A shot zoomed in tightly on one small detail, such as the eyes.

translations.ja: エクストリームクローズアップ

translations.es: a la altura de los ojos

words.meaning: A shot looking down on the subject, making them look small or helpless.

words.meaning: A shot looking up at the subject, making them look large or powerful.

words.meaning: The camera turns up or down while staying in one spot.

words.meaning: The lens brings the image closer or takes it further away while the camera stays still.

units.name: Barbie · Film techniques (CAMELS): editing, lighting and sound

words.meaning: The picture slowly turns to or from black, showing that time has passed.

words.meaning: One image slowly blends into the next.

words.meaning: Cutting back and forth between two events that are happening at the same time.

words.meaning: Dark lighting full of shadow, used to build suspense or unease.

words.meaning: Sound the characters themselves can hear, such as dialogue, footsteps or a car radio.

translations.ja: ダイジェティックサウンド

words.meaning: Sound only the audience hears, such as background music or a narrator.

translations.tl: tunog mula sa labas ng eksena

words.meaning: Everything placed in the shot (set, costume, props, lighting) and what it suggests.

words.meaning: An unfair judgement about someone, made before you know the facts.

words.meaning: Extra information in a sentence about when, where, how or why something happened.

units.name: Exploring Issues · Fact, opinion and bias

words.meaning: A statement that can be checked and proved true.
words.example: 'Voting is compulsory in Australia' is a fact you can check.

words.meaning: A personal belief or judgement that cannot be proved true or false.
words.example: 'The voting age should be lowered' is an opinion, however strongly it is argued.

words.meaning: A person or group with an interest in an issue, or affected by how it is decided.
words.example: List every stakeholder in the phone ban: students, teachers, families, the school.

words.meaning: Favouring one side of an issue unfairly instead of treating both sides evenly.
words.example: An article that quotes only one side shows bias.

words.meaning: The political party or side that a person, group or newspaper supports.
words.example: A paper's political affiliation can shape which stories reach the front page.

words.meaning: A headline written to make you click, often by exaggerating or leaving things out.
words.example: 'You won't believe what happened next' is clickbait, not news.

words.meaning: A feeling or idea a word suggests beyond its literal meaning.
words.example: 'Cheap' and 'affordable' cost the same, but the connotation is very different.

units.name: Exploring Issues · Persuasive techniques (PERSUADE)

words.meaning: A memory word for the eight persuasive techniques in this unit, from Power of three to Exaggeration.
words.example: Run PERSUADE over your draft: how many of the eight can you find?

words.meaning: Grouping three words or ideas together so the phrase has rhythm and sticks in the mind.
words.example: 'Safer, cheaper, fairer' uses the power of three.

words.meaning: Word choices picked to set off a strong feeling in the audience.
words.example: Calling a plan 'reckless' is emotive language; calling it 'untested' is not.

translations.vi: ngôn ngữ khơi gợi cảm xúc

words.meaning: A question asked for effect, where the answer is obvious and none is expected.
words.example: 'Do we really want dirtier air?' is a rhetorical question.

translations.ro: a căuta / a se îndrepta spre

words.meaning: Saying the same word or phrase again so the audience remembers it.
words.example: The repetition of 'not good enough' drives the point home.

words.meaning: Weakening the other side by attacking their argument, their evidence or their credibility.
words.example: Calling the other side 'out of touch' is an attempt to undermine the opposition.

words.meaning: A short personal story used to make an argument feel real.
words.example: She opens with an anecdote about her first week at a new school.

words.meaning: Speaking straight to the audience, usually with 'you' or 'your', to draw them in.
words.example: 'You pay for this every single week' is direct address.

translations.vi: cách nói trực tiếp với người đọc

words.meaning: Overstating something far beyond the truth for dramatic effect; also called hyperbole.
words.example: 'This will destroy our town forever' is exaggeration, not evidence.

words.meaning: Words like we, us and our that make the audience feel part of the writer's group.
words.example: Inclusive language turns one person's argument into something 'we' all share.

translations.zh-Hans: 包容性语言（我们、我们的）
translations.zh-Hant: 包容性語言（我們、我們的）

words.meaning: Numbers collected about many people or things, used as evidence in an argument.
words.example: Statistics sound solid, so always ask who collected them and how.

words.meaning: The view of someone who really knows the topic, used to give an argument authority.
words.example: Quoting a doctor is expert opinion; quoting a celebrity is not.

words.meaning: A reply that argues back against the other side's point.
words.example: Finish with a rebuttal so the other side's best point does not stand unanswered.

words.meaning: The main position a writer or speaker argues for — their one big idea.
words.example: State the contention in your first sentence, before any evidence.

units.name: Exploring Issues · Tone and connotation

words.meaning: The attitude a writer or speaker shows towards the subject, heard through word choice.
words.example: The tone shifts from calm to angry in the last paragraph.

words.meaning: The feeling or association a word carries on top of its dictionary meaning.
words.example: 'Slim' and 'skinny' describe the same body; only the connotation differs.

words.meaning: Expecting the worst outcome, and writing as though nothing will get better.
words.example: The pessimistic tone suggests that nothing will improve.

words.meaning: Showing intense and sincere feeling, as if the writer is boiling with it.
words.example: Her fervent tone tells you how much this issue matters to her.

words.meaning: Mocking; laughing at someone or something with contempt.
words.example: A derisive tone treats the opposing view as a joke.

words.meaning: Meant to calm anger and settle a disagreement.
words.example: A conciliatory tone can win over readers who started out disagreeing.

words.meaning: Speaking down to people as if they were less intelligent or less important.
words.example: 'Even a child could see this' is condescending.

words.meaning: Harshly critical, in words chosen to wound.
words.example: The editorial is scathing about the council's decision.

words.meaning: Saying the opposite of what you mean in order to mock or criticise.
words.example: 'What a brilliant plan' is sarcastic when the plan has just failed.

units.name: Exploring Issues · Spotting fake news and analysing visuals

translations.fr: une façon de faire quelque chose
translations.hi: किसी काम को करने का तरीका
translations.ro: un mod de a face ceva
translations.tl: paraan ng paggawa ng isang bagay
translations.ur: کسی کام کو کرنے کا طریقہ
translations.vi: cách làm một việc gì đó

words.meaning: A three-step way to analyse an image: See it, Explain it, then Analyse its effect.
words.example: Use the SEA method on the cartoon before you write a word about it.

translations.vi: phương pháp phân tích ảnh ba bước
translations.ur: تصویر تجزیے کا تین قدمی طریقہ
translations.ps: د انځور د شننې درې‌مرحله‌ییزه لاره
translations.ro: metoda SEA de analiză a imaginii
translations.es: método de análisis de imagen en tres pasos

words.meaning: The part of an image closest to the viewer, so the eye reaches it first.
words.example: The crying child in the foreground is what the photographer wants you to see.

words.meaning: The part of an image furthest from the viewer, which gives the scene its context.
words.example: Check the background: the empty shelves explain the whole photograph.

words.meaning: A photograph taken looking down on the subject, which can make them look small or weak.
words.example: The high-angle shot leaves the protesters looking outnumbered.

words.meaning: A photograph taken looking up at the subject, which can make them look powerful.
words.example: A low-angle shot turns an ordinary speaker into a giant.

words.meaning: Everything the maker chose to put inside the frame — and everything left out.
words.example: Describe the mise en scène: who is in the frame, and who is missing?

words.meaning: The line of text under or beside an image that tells you how to read it.
words.example: Cover the caption and the same photograph can mean something completely different.

words.meaning: A drawing that comments on a current issue or public figure, usually through exaggeration.
words.example: In the political cartoon the leader is drawn with a head twice the normal size.

words.meaning: A four-step check on information: Stop, Investigate the source, Find better coverage, Trace the claim.
words.example: Run SIFT on the post before you share it with anyone.

translations.vi: bốn bước kiểm chứng thông tin
translations.tl: apat na hakbang sa pagsusuri ng impormasyon
translations.ps: د معلوماتو د تاییدولو څلور ګامه

translations.zh-Hant: 阻止(如西洋棋中的將軍)
translations.ja: 止めること(チェスのチェックのように)
translations.vi: sự chặn lại (như trong cờ vua)

words.meaning: A website whose job is to test whether public claims are actually true.
words.example: A fact-checking site rated the claim as misleading.

translations.ja: ファクトチェックサイト

words.meaning: Searching with a picture instead of words, to find where that picture first appeared.
words.example: A reverse image search showed the flood photo was taken ten years earlier.

translations.vi: tìm kiếm ngược bằng hình ảnh

units.name: Exploring Issues · Appeals and analysis structure

words.meaning: Persuading by arguing that an idea will save the audience money, or cost them money.
words.example: An appeal to the hip-pocket nerve asks what the plan will do to your family's bills.

words.meaning: Persuading by tying an idea to the importance of family.
words.example: 'Think of your own children' is an appeal to family values.

translations.vi: kêu gọi giá trị gia đình

words.meaning: Persuading by arguing that an idea keeps the way things have always been done.
words.example: 'We have voted this way for a hundred years' is an appeal to tradition.

words.meaning: Persuading by making the audience feel worried, threatened or unsafe.
words.example: Crime figures on the front page are often an appeal to fear.

words.meaning: Persuading by framing an idea as fair and right, and the other side as unfair.
words.example: 'Everyone deserves the same chance' is an appeal to sense of justice.

words.meaning: Persuading by connecting an idea to pride in, and loyalty to, your own country.
words.example: The speech ends with an appeal to patriotism and a flag behind the speaker.

words.meaning: An analysis pattern: WHAT is argued, HOW language builds it, WHY it works on the audience.
words.example: Answer WHAT/HOW/WHY for one technique and you have a whole paragraph.

translations.ja: 何を・どう・なぜ分析

words.meaning: A checklist for introducing a text: Issue, Date, Author, Contention, Title, Form, Audience, Source, Tone.
words.example: Use IDACTFAST to write the opening sentences of your analysis.

translations.ja: 文章紹介チェックリスト
translations.vi: bảng kiểm giới thiệu văn bản

words.meaning: All the people entitled to vote in a particular area, or that area itself.
words.example: A member of parliament represents one electorate.

words.meaning: Parties joining forces to govern together; in Australia, the Liberal–National alliance.
words.example: No party won a majority, so a coalition formed government.

words.meaning: A system where citizens are required by law to vote.
words.example: Australia has compulsory voting; most other countries do not.

words.meaning: Websites and apps where people make, share and comment on each other's content.
words.example: The article argues that social media should be closed to under-sixteens.

translations.fr: transformé en / ayant la forme de
translations.ur: میں تبدیل شدہ / شکل رکھنے والا

words.meaning: A law that has been put forward for debate but has not been passed yet.
words.example: The proposed law would raise the age limit to sixteen.

words.meaning: A creator's legal right to control who copies or uses their work.
words.example: Training an AI on songs without permission raises copyright questions.

words.meaning: Tools, machines and systems built out of scientific knowledge.
words.example: Each article asks whether the technology is the problem, or the way we use it.

units.name: Literacy skills · Parts of speech 1: the word classes

words.meaning: A word that names a person, place, animal, thing, feeling or idea.
words.example: Underline every noun in the paragraph before you go looking for the verbs.

words.meaning: A noun that names a general kind of person, place or thing, not one particular one.
words.example: "City" is a common noun, so it does not need a capital letter.

words.meaning: A noun naming one particular person, place or thing, always written with a capital letter.
words.example: Every proper noun in your draft needs a capital letter.

words.meaning: A noun that names a whole group of people, animals or things as one unit.
words.example: "A herd of cattle" uses the collective noun "herd".

words.meaning: A noun naming an idea, quality or feeling you cannot touch, such as freedom.
words.example: "Courage" is an abstract noun: you can feel it, but you cannot hold it.

words.meaning: A word used in place of a noun, such as she, it or they.
words.example: Swap the repeated name for a pronoun so the sentence stops sounding clumsy.

words.meaning: A word that shows an action, a process, or a state of being.
words.example: Find the verb first and the subject of the sentence becomes easy to see.

words.meaning: A word that describes a noun, telling us what it is like.
words.example: Add one strong adjective to each noun, not three weak ones.

words.meaning: A word that describes a verb, an adjective or another adverb — often how, when or where.
words.example: "Badly" is an adverb telling us how the team played.

units.name: Literacy skills · Parts of speech 2: joining words, word parts and dictionary skills

words.meaning: A word showing how a noun relates to something else, often in place or time.
words.example: "On", "behind" and "throughout" are all prepositions.

words.meaning: A word that joins words, phrases or clauses together, such as and or because.
words.example: Use a conjunction to join those two short sentences into one.

words.meaning: In a dictionary, the word you are looking up, printed in bold at the start of the entry.
words.example: Find the given word in bold, then read the meaning beside it.

words.meaning: One of the two words at the top of a dictionary page showing the first and last entries on it.
words.example: Check the guiding words at the top before you turn another page.

words.meaning: A single beat of sound in a word.
words.example: Clap once for each syllable: "de-ten-tion" has three.

words.meaning: A word spelled and said the same as another word but with a completely different meaning.
words.example: "Can" is a homonym: you can sing, and you can open a can.

words.meaning: A word part fastened to the start of a word to change its meaning.
words.example: Adding the prefix "un-" to "happy" reverses the meaning.

words.meaning: A word part added to the end of a word to change its meaning or its grammar.
words.example: The suffix "-ful" turns the noun "hope" into the adjective "hopeful".

words.meaning: The simplest form of a word, before any prefix or suffix is added.
words.example: Strip off "un-" and "-ly" and the base word is "kind".

units.name: Literacy skills · Sentences and clauses

words.meaning: A group of words containing a subject and a verb.
words.example: Count the clauses: each one has its own subject and its own verb.

words.meaning: A clause that makes complete sense on its own and could stand alone as a sentence.
words.example: "The rain stopped" is an independent clause — it needs nothing else.

words.meaning: A clause that cannot stand alone; it needs an independent clause to make sense.
words.example: "Because the rain stopped" is a dependent/subordinate clause and leaves the reader waiting.

words.meaning: A sentence made of one independent clause and nothing else.
words.example: Write one simple sentence, then build it into a compound one.

words.meaning: A sentence joining two independent clauses, usually with a conjunction like and or but.
words.example: Join the two clauses with "but" to make a compound sentence.

words.meaning: A sentence joining an independent clause with one or more dependent clauses.
words.example: A complex sentence lets you show which of your two ideas matters most.

words.meaning: The capital letter and full stop that mark where a sentence begins and ends.
words.example: Half the marks here are for boundary punctuation, so check every capital and full stop.

units.name: Literacy skills · Punctuation and spelling

words.meaning: A punctuation mark showing a short pause, separating list items, or marking off extra information.
words.example: Put a comma between each item in the list, but not before the full stop.

words.meaning: A punctuation mark showing that something belongs to someone, as in "the driver's car".
words.example: One owner takes the apostrophe before the s; more than one takes it after.

translations.ja: 所有格アポストロフィ

words.meaning: A shortened form of two words, with an apostrophe standing in for the missing letters.
words.example: "Don't" is a contraction of "do not".

words.meaning: The exact words a person says, written inside speech marks.
words.example: Start a new line for each speaker when you write direct speech.

words.meaning: A letter or group of letters that stands for one sound.
words.example: The phonogram "igh" makes a single sound in "night".

words.meaning: Two or more consonants combined so that they make one distinct sound.
words.example: The consonant blend "kn" in "knee" hides a silent letter.

words.meaning: Two letters that together make a single sound.
words.example: "Th" and "ph" are digraphs: two letters, one sound.

words.meaning: Two vowels combined so that they make one sound.
words.example: The vowel blend "ea" in "beach" makes one long sound.

words.meaning: A word that sounds like another word but is spelled differently and means something else.
words.example: "To", "too" and "two" are homophones, so proofread for the right one.

words.meaning: A word with the same spelling and the same sound as another word, but a different meaning.
words.example: "Bat" is a homonym: an animal, or the thing you hit a ball with.

units.name: Literacy skills · Reading and writing: skimming, paragraphs and summarising

words.meaning: Reading quickly over a text to get its general idea.
words.example: Try skimming the first line of every paragraph before you read properly.

words.meaning: Reading quickly to find one particular piece of information.
words.example: Scanning the table for the date takes ten seconds, not ten minutes.

words.meaning: Reading in meaningful groups of words instead of one word at a time.
words.example: Chunking helps you read faster because your eyes stop fewer times.

words.meaning: The overall meaning of a text, once the extra detail is stripped away.
words.example: Give me the gist of the article in one sentence.

words.meaning: The sentence that states the main idea of a paragraph, usually the first one.
words.example: Your topic sentence should answer the question before you start proving it.

translations.ja: トピックセンテンス（主題文）

words.meaning: In a sentence, who or what the sentence is about — the doer of the verb.
words.example: In "the dog barked", the subject is "the dog".

words.meaning: In a sentence, the person or thing that the verb's action is done to.
words.example: In "the dog chased the cat", "the cat" is the object.

words.meaning: Cutting a longer text down to its most important ideas, in your own words.
words.example: Summarising a chapter in three sentences forces you to choose what matters.

units.name: Literacy skills · Speaking: debating

words.meaning: In a debate, the team that argues for the topic.
words.example: The affirmative speaks first and defines the topic.

words.meaning: In a debate, the team that argues against the topic.
words.example: The negative must challenge the definition straight away if they disagree with it.

words.meaning: The central argument a speaker or team is putting forward.
words.example: State your contention in one clear sentence before your first argument.

words.meaning: A short statement summing up a debating team's whole argument.
words.example: Every speaker repeats the team line so the adjudicator hears it three times.

words.meaning: How a debating team divides its arguments between its speakers.
words.example: Announce the team split so the audience knows what each speaker will cover.

words.meaning: Answering and knocking down the other team's arguments.
words.example: Spend the first minute on rebuttal, then move to your own case.

words.meaning: The person who judges a debate and decides which team has won.
words.example: The adjudicator gives feedback on matter, manner and method.

units.name: The Giver · Vocabulary list 1

words.meaning: So upset that you cannot think clearly.
words.example: Jonas is distraught when he learns what release really means.

words.meaning: To stick closely to a rule, a plan, or a surface.
words.example: Every family unit must adhere to the rules of the Community.

words.meaning: A natural ability or talent for something.
words.example: The Elders watch each child for an aptitude before giving out Assignments.

words.meaning: To tell someone off firmly for doing something wrong.
words.example: The speaker will chastise anyone who uses imprecise language.

words.meaning: To care for someone or something and help them grow.
words.example: Jonas begins to nurture Gabriel in secret.

words.meaning: To collect and store away a large supply of something, often secretly.
words.example: In a community built on Sameness, nobody is allowed to hoard anything.

words.meaning: Making you feel uneasy or worried.
words.example: There is something disquieting about a community with no colour in it.

words.meaning: A person's usual mood, or their natural way of behaving.
words.example: Fiona has a gentle disposition, which suits her work with the Old.

words.meaning: To laugh in a happy, chuckling way.
words.example: The younger children chortle at Asher's mixed-up words.

words.meaning: The ability to understand and share what another person is feeling.
words.example: The memories give Jonas an empathy no one else in the Community has.

words.meaning: Uncertain and not fully decided; done carefully, as a first try.
words.example: Jonas makes a tentative plan before he tells the Giver about it.

words.meaning: Extremely cold — cold enough to hurt.
words.example: The memory of the sled brings frigid air he has never felt before.

words.meaning: No longer used, because something newer has replaced it.
words.example: In the Community, words like "grandparent" have become obsolete.

units.name: The Giver · Vocabulary list 2

words.meaning: Gentle and harmless; causing no damage.
words.example: The Community looks benign until Jonas sees what lies under its rules.

words.meaning: Cheerful and confident, in a lively way.
words.example: Asher gives a jaunty wave as he rides off to his volunteer hours.

words.meaning: Lazy; avoiding any effort.
words.example: No citizen is allowed to be indolent, whatever their Assignment.

words.meaning: To make someone lose their confidence or their courage.
words.example: The silence of the Annex room begins to unnerve Jonas.

words.meaning: So painful that it is almost unbearable.
words.example: The memory of war is excruciating, and the Giver cannot take it back.

words.meaning: Very detailed and complicated, with many small parts.
words.example: The rules of the Community are more intricate than they first look.

words.meaning: Easy to notice, because it stands out from everything around it.
words.example: Jonas's pale eyes make him conspicuous among the other children.

words.meaning: To make someone curious or fascinated.
words.example: The Giver's memories intrigue Jonas long before they frighten him.

words.meaning: So strong that it feels as though you could touch it.
words.example: The tension in the Annex room is palpable.

words.meaning: Anxious that something bad is about to happen.
words.example: Jonas feels apprehensive on the morning of the Ceremony of Twelve.

words.meaning: To persuade someone by flattering them or gently pestering them.
words.example: Lily tries to wheedle one more story out of her father.

words.meaning: To go through something carefully, separating what matters from what does not.
words.example: Jonas has to sift through the memories to find the one he needs.

words.meaning: An act that breaks a rule or a moral code.
words.example: Even a small transgression is announced over the loudspeaker.

units.name: The Giver · Vocabulary list 3

words.meaning: To show itself clearly; plain and obvious.
words.example: Jonas's difference begins to manifest in the way he sees colour.

words.meaning: To fade away or grow weaker, little by little.
words.example: The Giver feels his strength ebb after each transmission.

words.meaning: Having no interesting or unusual features; easy to forget.
words.example: Every dwelling in the Community is deliberately nondescript.

words.meaning: To improve something, or make it better than it was.
words.example: Colour would enhance a world that has chosen to see only grey.

words.meaning: Added on to something else, to complete it or improve it.
words.example: The Giver gives Jonas supplementary rules that no other Twelve receives.

translations.ps: اضافي (چې د یو څه د بشپړولو یا ښه کولو لپاره ورزیات شوی)

words.meaning: Comfort at a time of sadness or worry.
words.example: Jonas finds solace in a memory of a family at Christmas.

words.meaning: To spread through something and fill every part of it.
words.example: Fear begins to permeate every conversation Jonas has at home.

words.meaning: Slow and relaxed, with very little energy.
words.example: The languid afternoon in the memory is unlike any day in the Community.

words.meaning: To become worn out and exhausted.
words.example: The endless rules frazzle anyone who tries to keep every one of them.

translations.fr: transformé en / ayant la forme de
translations.ur: میں تبدیل شدہ / شکل رکھنے والا

words.meaning: Sad and low in spirits after a disappointment.
words.example: Jonas comes back from the Annex dejected and silent.

words.meaning: Extremely careful and exact about small details.
words.example: The Community keeps meticulous records of every citizen.

words.meaning: To make a painful feeling less intense.
words.example: Nothing the Giver says can assuage Jonas's anger.

words.meaning: To take something in and make it part of you, or to fit into a new group.
words.example: Jonas has to assimilate a lifetime of memories in a single year.

units.name: The Giver · Vocabulary list 4

words.meaning: Sulky and bad-tempered, in a childish way.
words.example: Lily's petulant answer earns her a lesson in precise language.

translations.ja: 警告する/思い出させる

words.meaning: To tell someone off gently but firmly.
words.example: The loudspeaker will admonish anyone who breaks even a minor rule.

words.meaning: To become more serious or more intense.
words.example: A small lie can escalate into a serious transgression.

words.meaning: The great size or importance of something.
words.example: Jonas cannot grasp the magnitude of what the Giver carries alone.

words.meaning: An imagined society in which everything is perfect.
words.example: The Community is presented as a utopia until Jonas looks closely.

words.meaning: A group with intense, controlling devotion to one person or set of beliefs.
words.example: Some readers argue that the Community behaves like a cult.

words.meaning: Curving and winding, with many bends.
words.example: The river takes a sinuous path past the edge of the Community.

words.meaning: To hold something down by force, or stop it from being shown.
words.example: The Community works hard to suppress memory, colour and choice.

words.meaning: Full of energy and excitement.
words.example: The exuberant crowd in the memory is nothing like a Community ceremony.

words.meaning: To allow yourself, or someone else, a pleasure.
words.example: No citizen may indulge in anything the rules have not approved.

words.meaning: Giving off light; glowing.
words.example: The memory of sunshine leaves a luminous warmth Jonas cannot describe.

words.meaning: Done without any order or plan.
words.example: Nothing in the Community is haphazard; every detail has been decided.

translations.ja: 行き当たりばったりの

units.name: Two Wolves · Chapter vocabulary 1

words.meaning: Completely defeating someone or something.
words.example: The title asks which wolf inside you ends up vanquishing the other.

words.meaning: Thin, clear plastic wrapping that you can see through.
words.example: The sandwiches are still sealed in cellophane.

words.meaning: Behaving badly or breaking the law, especially a young person.
words.example: Ben worries that people will treat him as a delinquent because of his parents.

words.meaning: Far more of something than is needed.
words.example: Packing six torches for one night in the bush is overkill.

words.meaning: Lifted, pulled or threw something heavy, with a lot of effort.
words.example: Ben heaved his bag into the boot before anyone could look inside.

translations.ja: 力を込めて持ち上げた

words.meaning: To work out what something means and explain it.
words.example: Readers have to interpret Ben's silences as well as his words.

words.meaning: A body chemical released in fear or excitement that gives a sudden burst of energy.
words.example: Adrenaline keeps Ben running long after his legs want to stop.

words.meaning: Suddenly changed direction, often sharply and without warning.
words.example: The car veered off the highway onto a dirt track.

words.meaning: Rude, bad-tempered behaviour towards other people.
words.example: Olive notices her brother's surliness long before he explains it.

words.meaning: Having complete power; in everyday speech, very great or very loud.
words.example: There was an almighty crash from the shed behind the cabin.

words.meaning: Ran quickly, with short hurried steps.
words.example: A lizard scuttled away from the cabin steps.

units.name: Two Wolves · Chapter vocabulary 2

words.meaning: A strong, very unpleasant smell.
words.example: The stench from the old fridge fills the whole cabin.

words.meaning: Huge and frightening, like a monster.
words.example: In the dark, the gum tree by the track looks monstrous.

translations.fr: transformé en / ayant la forme de
translations.ur: میں تبدیل شدہ / شکل رکھنے والا

words.meaning: Thrown away because it was no longer wanted.
words.example: Discarded tins lie all around the old fire pit.

words.meaning: Spoke quietly and unclearly, usually in complaint.
words.example: Ben muttered something under his breath and kept walking.

words.meaning: Ran with short, quick steps, often out of fear.
words.example: A mouse scurried under the floorboards.

words.meaning: Certain to happen, as if it had been decided in advance.
words.example: Ben is afraid he is destined to repeat his father's mistakes.

words.meaning: Evil and cruel, like a villain in a story.
words.example: The novel never lets the parents become simply villainous.

words.meaning: Held back or smothered a sound, a feeling or a reaction.
words.example: Olive stifled a cough so the men outside would not hear her.

words.meaning: Badly made or worn out, and likely to break or collapse.
words.example: The rickety verandah shifts under their weight.

words.meaning: In an unclear or uncertain way.
words.example: Ben vaguely remembers the cabin from a holiday years before.

units.name: Two Wolves · Chapter vocabulary 3

words.meaning: Moving quickly to one side to avoid something.
words.example: Dodging the low branches, Ben runs deeper into the bush.

words.meaning: A narrow crack or gap, especially in rock.
words.example: He wedges the bag into a crevice above the river.

words.meaning: Poisonous, especially through a bite or a sting.
words.example: Most snakes out here are venomous, so they keep to the track.

words.meaning: Came out of somewhere and became visible.
words.example: A figure emerged from the trees on the far bank.

words.meaning: An amount of something gained or taken, usually after effort.
words.example: The haul in the bag is worth more than Ben wants to think about.

words.meaning: Stealing goods, especially by force.
words.example: The crows spend the morning plundering the campsite.

translations.ja: 法律を求める／提案する
translations.ro: a cere / a propune o lege

words.meaning: To question someone closely, and often aggressively.
words.example: Ben expects the police to interrogate his parents.

words.meaning: Faces up to someone or something directly, often in anger.
words.example: Ben finally confronts his father about the bag.

words.meaning: Waiting hidden, usually with a bad intention.
words.example: Something is lurking at the edge of the firelight.

words.meaning: Hints at an idea without stating it directly — a useful phrase for writing about a text.
words.example: The description of the cabin suggests that the family are not welcome there.

words.meaning: Having a rough, sharp, uneven edge.
words.example: A jagged rock cuts the rope as he pulls it up.

words.meaning: Moving suddenly and very quickly.
words.example: His eyes keep darting to the door.

words.meaning: An impressive display or range of things.
words.example: An array of camping gear is spread across the cabin floor.

words.meaning: Never stopping or easing off.
words.example: The heat in the bush is relentless by the middle of the day.

translations.fr: transformé en / ayant la forme de

words.meaning: Twisted and knotted, especially from age or weather.
words.example: A gnarled old tree leans out over the water.

words.meaning: Fierce, wild and violent.
words.example: A savage wind tears at the tent all night.

words.meaning: Making the harsh, loud call of a crow.
words.example: Crows are cawing from the dead branches above the camp.

words.meaning: Giving the feeling that something bad is about to happen.
words.example: The ominous quiet before the storm makes Olive nervous.

words.meaning: Made an angry, threatening growling sound.
words.example: The dog snarled at them from behind the wire.

words.meaning: To shake, especially from fear or cold.
words.example: Ben feels his hands quake as he unzips the bag.
